items.title: The weak topology of a normed space
items.statement: For K=R or C and normed X, sigma(X,X*) is the initial topology of all K-linear continuous f:X->K with the usual scalar topology. It agrees with the finite-neighborhood topology used in the published Mazur theorem. No completeness is assumed. Equivalently this is the topology pulled back from the product K^(X*) by x->(f(x))_f: product basic opens impose finitely many scalar tests.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon Example 3.8(i), p.122; Brezis §3.2 definition p.57

items.title: Finite weak neighborhoods and continuity of vector operations
items.statement: At x the sets U(x;f_1,...,f_m;epsilon)={y: |f_j(y-x)|<epsilon for every j}, m finite including zero and epsilon>0, form a base. They are convex and balanced at zero. Addition and scalar multiplication are continuous; sigma(X,X*) is coarser than norm topology.
items.proof_strategy: Initial-topology finite intersections refined by a common positive disk radius. Addition uses epsilon/2, scalar multiplication uses |a f(y)-a0 f(x)|<=|a||f(y-x)|+|a-a0||f(x)| for the finitely many coordinates. Norm continuity follows from boundedness of each f.

items.title: Weak topology is Hausdorff
items.statement: For real or complex normed X, sigma(X,X*) is Hausdorff.
items.proof_strategy: Separate x-y by a continuous functional and choose disjoint scalar disks around the two values. Pull them back.

items.title: Weak convergence of nets and sequences
items.statement: Write x_i -> x weakly iff f(x_i)->f(x) for every f in X*. This is equivalent to convergence in sigma(X,X*): directedness gives a common upper bound for the finitely many coordinate thresholds. Sequences use the usual directed order on N; closure is topological closure.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon Lemma 3.6(iii), p.121; net extension by finite directed upper bounds

items.title: The published weak-star topology and its predual
items.statement: Recall sigma(X*,X), already defined on the preceding A page, without rehoming or reminting def-weak-star-topology. On X*, sigma(X*,X) is coarser than sigma(X*,X**) and than norm topology, because evaluations belong to X**. The predual X is part of the notation.

items.title: Finite weak-star neighborhoods and Hausdorffness
items.statement: At f0 the sets {|(f-f0)(x_j)|<epsilon, 1<=j<=m} form a neighborhood base, m finite including zero. Sigma(X*,X) is Hausdorff, locally convex, with continuous addition and scalar multiplication.
items.proof_strategy: Reuse the published basis formula; inequalities for evaluations prove the vector operations as for weak neighborhoods. Distinct functionals differ on some x by their definition, without Hahn–Banach.

items.title: Weak-star convergence of nets
items.statement: A net f_i in X* converges weak-star to f iff f_i(x)->f(x) for every x in X. Finite directed upper bounds prove equivalence with topological convergence. Sequences are a special case, and never define closure.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon Example 3.9(iii), p.122; finite-coordinate net adaptation

items.title: Finite-coordinate factorization of a linear functional
items.statement: Let V be a K-vector space, f_1,...,f_m and L linear V->K, m finite including zero. If intersection ker f_j is contained in ker L then L=sum a_j f_j for some scalars a_j. Consequently the continuous linear dual of the initial topology generated by any family F of linear functionals is span F.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon Lemmas 3.13–3.14 and Theorem 3.12(i), pp.125–127; Brezis Lemma 3.2, p.64

items.proof_strategy: Factor L through E:V->K^m using the kernel condition. Extend the resulting functional on E(V) to K^m using a finite basis extension, and read its coefficients at standard vectors. For continuity at zero, a finite-coordinate neighborhood inside {|L|<1} forces L to vanish on its joint kernel by scaling. Conversely finite linear combinations are continuous. Empty family gives L=0. No infinite algebraic-dual extension. The finite basis of E(V) is obtained by adjoining outside its current span at most m times, as bounded by Steinitz; extend it by scanning the standard basis of K^m. No appeal to the AC-dependent general basis-extension theorem.

items.title: The weak continuous dual is the original dual
items.statement: The K-linear continuous functionals on (X,sigma(X,X*)) are exactly X*.
items.proof_strategy: Apply finite-coordinate factorization with F=X*, already a linear space. This proof also supplies the finite-span assertion needed for first countability.

items.title: Weak-star continuous functionals are evaluations
items.statement: Every K-linear sigma(X*,X)-continuous L:X*->K has the form L(f)=f(x) for a unique x in X. Conversely every evaluation is weak-star continuous. A nonempty affine hyperplane {f:L(f)=a}, with nonzero algebraic linear L, is weak-star closed iff L is evaluation at a vector of X. Completing a predual must not silently replace this topology: evaluations at completion vectors outside X are not weak-star continuous on X*.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon Corollary 3.25, p.130; Brezis Proposition 3.14, pp.64–65

items.proof_strategy: Factor through finitely many evaluations and put x=sum a_j x_j. Uniqueness uses dual separation; evaluation is bilinear with no complex conjugation. No Banach assumption or algebraic-dual identification. For a closed hyperplane translate to level 1 and take a balanced basic zero neighborhood disjoint from it. Scaling shows |L|<1 there (otherwise scale a point to level 1), hence continuity. Conversely continuous evaluations have closed level sets. The completion warning is conditional on the usual restriction identification of completion dual with X*: if evaluation at z in the completion were continuous, it would equal evaluation at some x in X; Hahn–Banach separation on the completion gives z=x. This warns against an identification, and does not use completion to prove the theorem.

items.title: Norm and weak closedness agree for convex sets
items.statement: For any convex C in a real or complex normed X, norm closure equals weak closure; in particular norm closed iff weakly closed, including C empty.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon Lemma 3.15, p.127; Brezis Theorem 3.7, pp.60–61

items.proof_strategy: Identify the exact finite-neighborhood topology of the published theorem with the initial topology using the basis lemma. Apply the published Mazur separation result. This is a topology dictionary, not a second separation theorem.

items.title: Weak neighborhoods in infinite dimension contain affine lines
items.statement: Every weak neighborhood of x in an infinite-dimensional normed X contains x+K v for some nonzero v, and is therefore norm unbounded.
items.proof_strategy: For m defining functionals choose m+1 linearly independent vectors by finitely many choices. Their coordinate images in K^m are dependent, giving a nonzero joint-kernel vector. Reverse triangle inequality proves unboundedness of the affine line.

items.title: Weak closure of the unit sphere
items.statement: In infinite-dimensional normed X, the weak closure of {x:||x||=1} is {x:||x||<=1}. The unit sphere of X* likewise has weak-star closure the dual closed unit ball when X is infinite dimensional.
items.proof_strategy: The closed ball is convex and norm closed. For ||x||<1, a weak neighborhood contains x+R v with v nonzero. The continuous function t->||x+tv|| crosses 1 by the intermediate value theorem; ||x||=1 is immediate. No assertion about sequences. Dual separation forces X* infinite dimensional (a finite spanning family would embed X into a finite coordinate space). Apply the primal assertion to X*. Its weak topology is finer than weak-star, while the dual closed ball is weak-star closed as the intersection |f(x)|<=||x|| for x in X. These two inclusions prove the dual assertion.

items.title: Sequential uniform boundedness using countable choice
items.statement: Assume AC_omega. A pointwise bounded sequence T_n:E->F of bounded linear operators, E Banach and F normed over R or C, has sup_n ||T_n|| finite.

references.title: Sokal, A Really Simple Elementary Proof of the Uniform Boundedness Theorem, p.2, displayed (2) and proof

items.proof_strategy: If norms are unbounded let k_j be the least index with ||T_kj||>=4^j. AC_omega chooses once for all j vectors u_j with ||u_j||<=3^(-j) and ||T_kj u_j||>(2/3)3^(-j)||T_kj||. Starting z_0=0, set z_j=z_(j-1)+s_j u_j where s_j is +1 if that image norm is at least the minus alternative, and -1 otherwise. The triangle inequality gives ||T_kj z_j||>=||T_kj u_j||. This sign rule is deterministic, so needs no DC. Completeness and the geometric tail give z_j->z and ||z-z_j||<=3^(-j)/2. Thus ||T_kj z||>(1/6)(4/3)^j, contradiction. Explicitly label this as an adaptation of Sokal rather than claiming the source states the AC_omega refinement.

items.title: Weakly convergent sequences are norm bounded
items.statement: Assume AC_omega in addition to the inherited Hahn–Banach machinery. If x_n converges weakly in a normed X, sup_n ||x_n||<infinity. X itself need not be complete. Also if f_n->f in dual norm, then f_n(x_n)->f(x).

references.title: Brezis Proposition 3.5(iii), p.58 (completeness needed only for the dual)

items.proof_strategy: Apply the sequential lemma to J_X x_n:X*->K. The domain X* is Banach even for incomplete X, scalar convergence supplies pointwise boundedness, and ||J_X x_n||=||x_n||. No general-family Baire or DC theorem is used. For the last assertion use |f_n(x_n)-f(x)|<=||f_n-f|| sup_k||x_k||+|f(x_n-x)|.

items.title: The norm is weakly lower semicontinuous
items.statement: For every weakly convergent net x_i->x, ||x||<=liminf_i ||x_i||, with liminf=sup_i inf_{j>=i} in the extended nonnegative reals. Every norm sublevel set is weakly closed. More generally every convex extended-real norm-lower-semicontinuous function is weakly lower semicontinuous, where lower semicontinuity means closed real sublevel sets.

references.title: Brezis Proposition 3.5(iii), p.58; net form by the same dual norm estimate

items.proof_strategy: For any real a<||x|| choose a norming functional at nonzero x; eventually |f(x_i)|>a, so eventually ||x_i||>a. Handle x=0 directly. Equivalently use the intersection {|f(x)|<=r:||f||<=1}. No boundedness assertion for nets. Its sublevel sets are convex and norm closed, hence weakly closed by the earlier convex closure theorem.

items.title: Equality of weak and norm topologies characterizes finite dimension
items.statement: The weak and norm topologies of a real or complex normed X agree iff X is finite-dimensional.
items.proof_strategy: A chosen finite basis has bounded coordinate functionals; coordinate-small implies norm-small. Treat X=0. Conversely a norm ball cannot be a weak neighborhood by the affine-line lemma.

items.title: Weak topology in infinite dimension is not first countable
items.statement: Assume AC_omega and the inherited dual-separation principle. The weak topology of an infinite-dimensional normed X is not first countable at zero (hence at any point).

references.title: Brezis Exercise 3.8(1)–(3), p.81; local-base version and published ZF no-countable-basis route

items.proof_strategy: Given a countable local base choose a basic finite-coordinate refinement in each member using AC_omega; include an ordered tuple in each selected datum. Flatten these tuples to a sequence. For each f in X*, a refinement inside {|f|<1} and scaling imply f lies in the finite span of its coordinates. Greedily retain the first linearly independent terms, deterministically. If infinitely many are retained they form a countably infinite Hamel basis of the Banach space X*, contradicting the published proved theorem (not the recorded remark). Thus finitely many span X*. Dual separation embeds X into their finite coordinate space, contradiction.

items.title: Annihilators are closed in the appropriate weak topology
items.statement: For arbitrary M subset X and N subset X*, M-perp is sigma(X*,X)-closed and preannihilator N is sigma(X,X*)-closed; both are linear subspaces.
items.proof_strategy: Intersect kernels of the defining continuous evaluations/functionals. Empty sets give the whole ambient space.

items.title: The two double-annihilator closure formulas
items.statement: Reuse the published theorem: preannihilator(M-perp)=norm closure M=weak closure M for linear M<=X, while (preannihilator N)-perp=weak-star closure N for linear N<=X*. Do not replace the last closure by norm closure. The canonical map J_X is continuous from weak X to weak-star X** since (J_X x)(f)=f(x); dual separation makes it a topological embedding onto its image by the identical finite test bases.

items.title: Bounded maps and their transposes are weak-to-weak continuous
items.statement: For bounded T:X->Y between normed spaces, T:(X,weak)->(Y,weak) is continuous, and T*:(Y*,sigma(Y*,Y**))->(X*,sigma(X*,X**)) is continuous.
items.proof_strategy: For each g in Y*, g composed with T=T*g is in X*. Apply the same observation to bounded T*, using its transpose T** on testing bidual functionals. Initial topology proves continuity for all nets.

items.title: Weak-star continuity and the unique bounded preadjoint
items.statement: For normed X,Y, bounded T:X->Y has weak-star continuous transpose T*:Y*->X*. Conversely a bounded weak-star continuous K-linear S:Y*->X* equals T* for a unique bounded T:X->Y, with ||T||<=||S|| (hence equality by transpose norm equality).

references.title: Brezis Exercise 3.10 p.81 and Proposition 3.14 pp.64–65, combined preadjoint consequence

items.proof_strategy: Forward: (T*g)(x)=g(Tx). Converse: for each x, g->(Sg)(x) is weak-star continuous, hence g(Tx) for a unique Tx in Y. Uniqueness gives a well-defined map and linearity without any global choice. The dual norm formula gives ||Tx||=sup_{||g||<=1}|(Sg)(x)|<=||S||||x||. Separation gives uniqueness of T. No reflexivity or completeness.

items.title: Strong and weak operator topologies
items.statement: On B(X,Y), SOT is the initial topology of T->Tx into normed Y for all x in X; WOT is the initial topology of T->g(Tx) into K for x in X,g in Y*. Thus nets converge in SOT iff pointwise in norm and in WOT iff pointwise weakly. Finite tests form neighborhood bases; neither is named simply the weak topology of B(X,Y).

references.title: Feldman, Operator Topologies, Definition 1 p.1; Banach-space/net adaptation

items.title: Operator norm convergence implies SOT implies WOT
items.statement: For nets of bounded operators between normed spaces, operator norm convergence implies SOT convergence, which implies WOT convergence.
items.proof_strategy: Use ||(T_i-T)x||<=||T_i-T||||x|| and |g((T_i-T)x)|<=||g||||(T_i-T)x|| at each fixed x,g.

title: Weak and Weak Star Topologies — Examples

items.title: Coordinate vectors are weakly null in ell-p
items.statement: For real ell^p, 1<p<infinity, e_n converges weakly to 0 although ||e_n||_p=1.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon Exercise 3.60(a) p.161 (ell-two case); Example 1.34 pp.34–35 (ell-p extension)

items.proof_strategy: Its dual is real ell^q with q finite. Each testing coefficient b_n tends to zero, since sum |b_n|^q is finite. State the real scope of MT-16 explicitly.

items.title: Coordinate vectors are not weakly null in ell-one
items.statement: The coordinate vectors of real ell^1 do not converge weakly to 0.
items.proof_strategy: The bounded functional x->sum x_n, represented by constant one in ell-infinity, takes value 1 on every e_n.

items.title: Coordinate evaluations on ell-one are weak-star null
items.statement: In real (ell^1)*=ell-infinity, f_n(x)=x_n converges weak-star to zero, with ||f_n||=1.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon Example 3.9(iii), p.122 and Example 1.35, p.36

items.proof_strategy: Absolute summability gives x_n->0 for each fixed x. The coordinate vector tests give the operator norm. This is a sequence in ell-infinity, not ell-one.

items.title: Weak-star and weak topologies differ on c-zero dual
items.statement: In real ell^1=(c0)*, e_n tends weak-star to zero but not weakly to zero.
items.proof_strategy: For x in c0 the pairing is x_n->0; the ell-infinity constant-one functional on ell^1 takes value 1. Name both pairings separately.

items.title: A weak closure point unattainable by sequences
items.statement: In real ell^2, A={sqrt(n+1)e_n:n>=0} is sequentially weakly closed, but 0 belongs to its weak closure and not to A.
items.proof_strategy: For finitely many dual sequences b^j in ell^2, if every n had max_j sqrt(n+1)|b^j_n|>=epsilon, then sum_n sum_j |b^j_n|^2>=epsilon^2 sum_n 1/(n+1)=infinity. Prove the latter divergence inline by dyadic blocks, so no B-homed harmonic example is a dependency. Thus every weak neighborhood of zero meets A. A weakly convergent sequence in A has bounded norms by the A theorem; its indices lie in a finite set, whose only possible limits are its members by Hausdorffness. Do not use the unit sphere or Hilbert Riesz.

items.title: Right shifts converge in WOT but not SOT
items.statement: On real ell^2, R(x_0,x_1,...)=(0,x_0,x_1,...) has R^n->0 in WOT but not SOT.
items.proof_strategy: The pairing with b in ell^2 is bounded by ||x||_2 times the norm of the tail (b_n,b_(n+1),...). Derive Cauchy–Schwarz from sum(s x_k-t b_k)^2>=0 on finite prefixes and limits if needed. R^n preserves ||x||, excluding SOT at nonzero x.

items.title: Left shifts converge in SOT but not operator norm
items.statement: On real ell^2, L(x_0,x_1,...)=(x_1,x_2,...) has L^n->0 in SOT and ||L^n||=1.
items.proof_strategy: The squared norm is the squared-sum tail. Test e_n to attain norm 1. Include tail projections as another explicit SOT-but-not-norm example from the same calculation.

items.title: Weak-star convergence on an incomplete predual does not bound norms
items.statement: Let E=c00 with supremum norm and f_n(x)=(n+1)x_n. Then f_n converges weak-star to zero in E*, but ||f_n||=n+1. In particular pointwise boundedness on incomplete E does not bound operator norms.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon Example 2.6 p.61, combined with Example 3.9(iii) p.122

items.proof_strategy: Finite support makes each scalar sequence eventually zero. Test e_n for the norm. Truncations of (2^(-k)) are sup-norm Cauchy with no limit in c00. Recompute the earlier B-page example, adding the new weak-star consequence; do not cite that B-homed item as a dependency.

items.title: A weakly null net with no norm-bounded tail
items.statement: Every infinite-dimensional normed space has a weakly null net whose norms tend to infinity; no tail is norm bounded.

references.title: Brezis §3.2 Example 1 footnote 2, p.59; explicit net adaptation of unbounded weak neighborhoods

items.proof_strategy: Index by all triples (U,m,x), U a basic weak neighborhood of zero, m in N, x in U and ||x||>m. Preorder triples by reverse inclusion in U and increasing m. Every finite intersection is a weak neighborhood and norm unbounded, so this is a nonempty directed preorder. Send the triple to its own x. Given U0, a tail has U subset U0; given M, a tail has m>M. Include x in the index rather than choosing one point for each U,m. The published definition permits preorders; no antisymmetry repair is needed.
